name: Network Infrastructure Configuration
weakness: An unauthenticated Redis instance is published to the host, and backend infrastructure services are reachable from the edge network.

name: Application Platform Configuration
weakness: Default 'It works!' page, vendor sample content and platform-wide directory listing left enabled.

name: File Extensions Handling for Sensitive Information
weakness: Sensitive extensions are served as text/plain; PHP source is disclosed because no handler is configured.

name: Review Old Backup and Unreferenced Files for Sensitive Information
weakness: A real tarball backup containing .env and secrets, editor swap files, .DS_Store and a decommissioned admin directory with credentials are all retrievable.

name: Enumerate Infrastructure and Application Admin Interfaces
weakness: Adminer, Apache server-status/server-info and nginx stub_status are exposed without authentication; the app admin login accepts default credentials.

name: HTTP Methods
weakness: TraceEnable On echoes requests; anonymous WebDAV allows PUT/DELETE/MKCOL on both nginx and Apache.

name: HTTP Strict Transport Security
weakness: HTTPS is served without Strict-Transport-Security, and HTTP serves the application instead of redirecting to TLS.

name: File Permissions
weakness: Upload directory is 0777 (world-writable), secret config is 0644 (world-readable), and the web root is writable by the anonymous WebDAV user.

name: Subdomain Takeover
weakness: A deprovisioned SaaS site left a live CNAME. The provider returns the characteristic unclaimed-host 404 and lets anyone claim the hostname, completing a real takeover.

name: Cloud Storage
weakness: An S3 bucket carries a public-read ACL and an Allow Principal:* policy, and anonymous callers can read customer PII and a portal .env from it. A sibling bucket is correctly marked private.
degraded: LocalStack's S3 does not enforce authorization for anonymous requests, so the private sibling bucket cannot be shown returning 403. Bucket ACL/policy inspection and the anonymous public exposure of PII are faithful; the enforcement contrast is not.

name: Content Security Policy
weakness: CSP uses 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval' and wildcard sources; other pages send no CSP at all.

name: Path Confusion
weakness: nginx alias traversal escapes the static root; a slash-less proxy prefix lets /apiadmin/users bypass the deny rule on /admin; merge_slashes off adds a further normalisation gap.

name: Additional Browser Security Controls
weakness: X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and the Cross-Origin-* policies are all absent.

name: Feature Flag Security Bypass
weakness: The full feature-flag inventory is public and a privileged console is gated on a client-controlled cookie/header rather than the user's role.

name: Web Cache Poisoning
weakness: Varnish keys the cache on URL only while the backend reflects X-Forwarded-Host into a cacheable response, so one poisoned request is served to all later visitors.

name: Conduct Search Engine Reconnaissance for Information Leakage
weakness: Secret-bearing pages (config backups, .env, decommissioned admin notes) are indexable; robots.txt advertises them. An in-range crawler/search index stands in for a public engine.
degraded: In-range search index replaces a public search engine; the lab performs no outbound queries. Dorking syntax (site:/inurl:/intitle:) and the leaked-content outcome are faithful.

name: Fingerprint Web Server
weakness: server_tokens on (nginx) and ServerTokens Full (Apache) disclose exact versions in headers and error pages.

name: Review Webserver Metafiles for Information Leakage
weakness: Metafiles enumerate hidden paths, allow any RIA cross-domain access, and leak internal hosts and a stale security contact.

name: Attack Surface Identification
weakness: Nine published ports across proxy, cache, admin, DNS, S3 and an unauthenticated datastore, plus a sitemap enumerating unlinked paths.

name: Review Web Page Content for Information Leakage
weakness: HTML comments carry DB credentials and internal IPs; hidden fields carry a tenant id; inline JS hardcodes a live API key.

name: Identify Application Entry Points
weakness: GET and POST entry points with reflected parameters, hidden fields, and header/cookie-driven behaviour are all discoverable from the homepage.

name: Map Execution Paths Through Application
weakness: A three-hop link chain reaches a data-export endpoint that is never linked from the homepage, so only path mapping finds it.

name: Fingerprint Web Application Framework
weakness: Werkzeug/Flask error pages disclose the framework and its exact version.

name: Fingerprint Web Application
weakness: Application name, version and build number are disclosed in a meta generator tag, a response header and a public changelog.

name: Map Application Architecture
weakness: Proxy, cache, application and database tiers each identify themselves through headers and responses, allowing the full architecture to be mapped from outside.

name: Credentials Transported over an Encrypted Channel
weakness: Login form posts credentials over cleartext HTTP with an absolute http:// action; no TLS, no HSTS, no redirect to HTTPS.

name: Default Credentials
weakness: Seeded default credentials admin/admin, admin/password and operator/operator all authenticate successfully.

name: Weak Lock Out Mechanism
weakness: Lockout bucket is keyed on the client-controlled X-Forwarded-For header; rotating it bypasses the lock, and reset_counter=1 clears the failure counter.

name: Bypassing Authentication Schema
weakness: Authenticated page trusts a client-supplied authenticated=true parameter/cookie, granting admin account data (incl. api_key) with no session.

name: Vulnerable Remember Password
surface: POST /login remember=1, GET /account with remember_me cookie
weakness: Remember-me cookie is base64(username:password); it decodes to cleartext credentials and replays as full authentication in a fresh session.

name: Browser Cache Weaknesses
weakness: Authenticated sensitive page is sent with Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600 (no no-store/no-cache), so browsers and shared proxies cache account data and api_key.

name: Weak Authentication Methods
weakness: HTTP Basic authentication is offered over cleartext HTTP, and a GET-based login accepts credentials in the URL query string.

name: Weak Security Question Answer
weakness: Security-question answers have a tiny space (default 'smith', also 'fluffy') and the answer endpoint has no rate limiting, so brute force succeeds and yields a reset token.

name: Weak Password Change or Reset Functionalities
weakness: Reset tokens are short sequential 4-digit numbers (predictable), never expire, are reusable, require no old password, and the reset link is built from the request Host header (host-header poisoning).

name: Weaker Authentication in Alternative Channel
weakness: The mobile API channel accepts Basic auth with no MFA and no lockout for an MFA-enabled account that the web channel blocks, and survives unlimited failed attempts.

name: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
weakness: Post-MFA page only checks login (jump straight to /mfa/dashboard pre-verification); TOTP seed is predictably derived from the username and backup codes are enumerable (000001..).

name: SAML Authentication
weakness: Hand-built SP accepts unsigned SAML assertions, ignores Audience/NotOnOrAfter (expired+wrong-audience accepted), and reads NameID via naive .text so XML comment injection (admin<!---->@corp) truncates to admin. Keycloak is the real configured IdP.

name: Passkeys and WebAuthn
weakness: Weak RP: user_verification=discouraged (no-UV software credential accepted), attestation=none with no validation, a single static challenge not bound to the session (assertion accepted in a fresh session), and unauthenticated credential-id enumeration.

name: OpenID Connect Relying Party
weakness: RP decodes ID tokens without signature verification (alg=none accepted), never checks nonce/state, and validates redirect_uri by substring match, leaking tokens in the URL fragment to a third-party host. Real Keycloak OIDC tokens are also accepted.

name: Role Definitions
weakness: Role matrix exposes undocumented wildcard roles (superadmin, root); registration honours a client-supplied role, so any user self-assigns superadmin and reaches the admin panel with permissions ['*'].

name: User Registration Process
weakness: No email verification (account instantly active), disposable domains accepted, and no UNIQUE constraint allows duplicate/race registration of the same username into multiple rows.

name: Account Provisioning Process
weakness: Unauthenticated bulk-provision endpoint creates accounts with sequential predictable ids and a known default password (Welcome123!); accounts are readable by guessing id+1.

name: Account Enumeration and Guessable User Account
weakness: Login/registration/reset return distinguishable 'existing user' vs 'no such user' responses; guessable accounts admin/administrator/test are seeded.

name: Weak or Unenforced Username Policy
weakness: No username policy: empty, single-character, unicode and space-only usernames are all accepted at registration.

name: Directory Traversal and File Include
weakness: Download endpoint joins user input to the docroot with no containment check (../, ..%2f and absolute paths read /srv/secret/flag.txt); sibling fetch endpoint filters '../' once then URL-decodes, so ....// and double-encoded ..%252f bypass it.

name: Bypassing Authorization Schema
surface: GET /admin/users, POST /admin/announce, GET vs POST /admin/export, GET /admin/panel + POST /admin/settings
weakness: Forced browsing to an unchecked admin API; admin POST action with no server-side check; GET /admin/export enforces admin but POST does not (method switching); admin panel role check exists only in client-side JS and the settings POST trusts a client-supplied role field.

name: Privilege Escalation
weakness: Mass assignment: the profile-update handler copies a user-supplied 'role' field into the account, letting a normal user become admin and pass the real server-side check on /admin.

name: Insecure Direct Object References
weakness: Sequential object ids are readable and writable across users (documents, orders); a public user-list response leaks per-user UUID inbox references which are then readable without ownership checks.

name: OAuth Weaknesses / OAuth Authorization Server Weaknesses / OAuth Client Weaknesses
weakness: 05.1 AS: redirect_uri validated by substring (attacker host and path-traversal URIs pass), codes replayable, expired codes accepted, code not bound to client_id, scope escalation to admin without consent, client_secret accepted in URL query. 05.2 client: no state (login CSRF), PKCE downgrade, open redirect, access token leaked via Referer to in-range host, implicit-flow token in URL fragment.

name: Session Management Schema
surface: Set-Cookie SID on GET / and POST /login
weakness: Session ids are a plain sequential counter; the next id is predictable and a pre-set predicted id becomes another user's authenticated session after their login.

name: Cookies Attributes
weakness: Session cookie is set with Path=/ only: no HttpOnly, no Secure, no SameSite attribute.

name: Session Fixation
surface: GET / with attacker-chosen SID, then POST /login
weakness: Server adopts any client-supplied session id and does not rotate it on login, so a fixated id survives authentication and authenticates the victim's session to the attacker.

name: Exposed Session Variables
surface: GET /api/me?sid=, GET /dashboard?sid= (hidden field + third-party img), Referer to :8320/pixel
weakness: Session id accepted in the URL query, embedded in a hidden form field, and leaked to an in-range third-party host through the Referer header of an embedded image.

name: Cross Site Request Forgery
weakness: State-changing transfer has no CSRF token, no Origin/Referer check and no SameSite cookie; a cross-origin form post carrying only the session cookie moves funds.

name: Logout Functionality
surface: POST /logout, then GET /api/me with the old SID
weakness: Logout only expires the client cookie; the server-side session record is never invalidated and the old id keeps authenticating.

name: Session Timeout
weakness: No idle or absolute timeout exists in policy or code; a session backdated 30 days (lab knob simulates elapsed time) still authenticates.

name: Session Puzzling
weakness: The password-reset flow writes the same session['user'] variable the authenticated area trusts, so completing a reset for 'admin' enters an admin context without ever supplying a password.

name: Session Hijacking
surface: GET /api/me + /documents/1 with a stolen SID from a different client context
weakness: Predictable session id transmitted over plain HTTP with no binding to User-Agent or client IP; replaying a derived id from a different client context hijacks the session and reads private objects.

name: JSON Web Tokens
weakness: API accepts alg=none unsigned tokens, signs with the weak HMAC secret 'secret' (brute-forced from an 8-word list to forge an admin token), and never validates exp/aud/iss (expired tokens accepted).

name: Concurrent Sessions
surface: 5x POST /login, POST /account/password, GET /api/me on every session
weakness: No concurrent-session limit and a password change invalidates zero sessions: five simultaneous sessions for one account all survive the password change.

name: SQL Injection / Oracle / MySQL / SQL Server / PostgreSQL / MS Access / NoSQL Injection / ORM Injection / Client-side
weakness: One vulnerable endpoint per dialect, each concatenating input into queries against real MySQL 8.4, PostgreSQL 16, MSSQL 2022, MongoDB 7 and SQLite engines: UNION/boolean-blind/stacked/LOAD_FILE (MySQL), || concatenation + pg_sleep (PostgreSQL), UNION + batched WAITFOR (MSSQL), mod_plsql gateway dynamic SQL (Oracle facade), Jet IIF/TOP/#date#/stacked facade (Access), $where + operator injection via JSON and bracket query-string (NoSQL), SQLAlchemy filter/order_by text() fragments (ORM), alasql URL-parameter concatenation in the browser (client-side). Every dialect extracts a seeded secret row.
degraded: 05.1 Oracle: gvenzl/oracle-xe:21-slim exists on the mirror but is amd64-only and the Oracle engine cannot run on arm64 (unsupported under Rosetta) - faithful mod_plsql/ORDS gateway surface (/pls/<dad>/<package>.<proc>) with the Oracle engine substituted by PostgreSQL. 05.5 MS Access: no Linux Jet/ACE engine exists - Access-dialect facade (IIF/TOP/*-wildcards/#date#/stacked ';') over real SQLite. All other dialects run against real servers.

name: LDAP Injection
weakness: Search filter built by concatenation (&(uid=<input>)(userPassword=<input>)) against real OpenLDAP 2.6; *)(uid=*))(|(uid=* and * enumerate all entries and disclose passwords and the admin secret attribute without authentication.

name: XML Injection
weakness: Order envelope built by string concatenation: injecting </item><price>0</price> changes the document structure and the charged total (200 -> 0). /xml/parse resolves external entities (file:// only, network disabled), disclosing a seeded secret file via XXE.

name: XPath Injection
weakness:
Authentication XPath //user[login/text()='' and password/text()='

'] built by concatenation over an XML user store; ' or '1'='1 bypasses authentication and extracts every user node including the admin secret.

name: JSON Parser Differentials
weakness: Front validator parses JSON first-wins and authorises on that view, then forwards raw bytes to a backend that parses last-wins: {"role":"user","role":"admin"} passes the front as user while the backend grants the admin-only secret. Unicode-escaped duplicate keys (ro\u006ce) produce the same differential.

name: Reflected Cross Site Scripting
weakness: The search parameter is echoed without encoding into three distinct contexts: HTML body, an HTML attribute value and a JavaScript string literal, so each needs a different breakout payload.

name: Stored Cross Site Scripting
surface: POST :8500/guestbook (author=, comment=) then GET /guestbook; POST /profile (bio=) then GET /profile
weakness: Guestbook comments and profile bios are persisted in SQLite and rendered unescaped to every later visitor; the bio also lands inside a JS string literal.

name: HTTP Verb Tampering
weakness: Admin access control is enforced only for GET and POST, so PUT/PATCH/HEAD and arbitrary verbs reach the protected handler; the nginx WAF rule likewise inspects only GET query strings.

name: HTTP Parameter Pollution
weakness: nginx authorises on the first occurrence of role while the Flask handler takes the last; the transfer gateway validates the first body occurrence and forwards the raw body to an internal backend that takes the last.

name: SSI Injection
surface: GET :8505/cgi-bin/greet.cgi?name=<!--#exec cmd="id"--> then GET the returned /pages/*.shtml
weakness: Apache mod_include with Options +Includes and AddOutputFilter INCLUDES .shtml; a CGI writes user input verbatim into a .shtml page, so injected SSI echo/exec directives are executed by the server.

name: Code Injection / File Inclusion
weakness: PHP eval() and call_user_func() execute attacker-supplied code; include() has no path validation and allow_url_include=On, giving LFI, php://filter source disclosure, log poisoning and RFI against an in-range host.

name: Command Injection
weakness: A ping utility concatenates input into a shell command (subprocess shell=True and PHP shell_exec); a second lookup utility discards output, leaving a time-based blind channel.

name: Server-side Template Injection
weakness: User input is concatenated into the template source itself: Flask render_template_string (Jinja2) and Mako Template(). Both evaluate attacker expressions and reach OS command execution.

name: Prototype Pollution
surface: POST :8520/settings {"__proto__":{...}} then GET /admin, GET /profile, POST /render on new connections
weakness: A hand-rolled recursive merge with no own-property guard writes into Object.prototype via __proto__ and constructor.prototype; later unrelated requests inherit isAdmin=true and ejs 3.1.6 picks up a polluted outputFunctionName for RCE.

name: Unicode Normalization and Case Mapping
weakness: Path blacklist, authorisation equality, SQL keyword filter and XSS filter all run before NFKC normalization / casefold, so fullwidth characters and U+017F long-s fold back into the blocked ASCII forms at the sink.

name: IMAP SMTP Injection
weakness: User input is concatenated into SMTP MAIL FROM/RCPT TO and IMAP SELECT commands; CRLF injection adds an extra recipient (delivered by Mailpit) and an extra IMAP CREATE command (executed by Dovecot).

name: Buffer Overflow / Format String Injection
weakness: Native C service compiled -fno-stack-protector -z execstack -no-pie: strcpy overflows a 64-byte buffer into an adjacent canary (and crashes on long input); printf(user_input) leaks stack pointers (%p), reads arbitrary strings (%s) and writes memory (%n).

name: Incubated Vulnerability
weakness: A filename is stored benignly (HTML-escaped, no execution) by the portal, then later concatenated into a shell command by a separate export worker, detonating the incubated payload (id output + in-range callback).

name: HTTP Response Splitting
weakness: A legacy raw-socket service writes the decoded lang parameter verbatim into Set-Cookie without stripping CR/LF, so %0d%0a injects an extra header or a whole second response.

name: HTTP Request Smuggling
surface: POST :8616 (CL-framing proxy) with obfuscated Transfer-Encoding + innocent GET on same connection
weakness: The front proxy frames by Content-Length only while the backend honours obfuscated Transfer-Encoding (xchunked) as chunked; the CL.TE desync lets a smuggled prefix poison the next request, which receives the smuggled response.

name: Host Header Injection
weakness: Absolute reset links are built from Host/X-Forwarded-Host (attacker host reflected), duplicate Host headers are accepted, and a cache keyed on URL only serves a Host-poisoned response to later visitors.

name: Server-Side Request Forgery
weakness: URL fetcher has no allowlist: reaches an internal-only unpublished service, a cloud-metadata-style endpoint on 169.254.169.254 (fake IAM creds), reads local files via file:// and speaks gopher:// to internal hosts.

name: Mass Assignment
weakness: The model binder binds every supplied JSON field, so a normal user escalates by adding is_admin/role/balance the UI never sends, then reads the admin-only flag.

name: CSV Injection
weakness: The CSV export writes user-controlled cells unescaped, so =cmd|... (DDE) and =HYPERLINK(...) prefixes survive as formulas; opening the export interprets them and the HYPERLINK exfiltrates to an in-range listener.
degraded: Spreadsheet client is simulated by the in-range csv-open service (no headless Excel available); the unescaped formula export and HYPERLINK exfil to an in-range listener are faithful, DDE commands are recorded rather than executed.

name: Insecure Deserialization
weakness: Python pickle.loads() and PHP unserialize() (no allowed_classes) accept attacker payloads: a pickle __reduce__ chain executes code (reads flag/id) and a PHP Report->Reader __toString POP chain reads the flag while Executor __destruct runs shell commands.

name: Server-side URL Redirect
weakness: The SERVER validates redirect targets (substring/relative-path checks) and fetches them server-side, but //evil, %2f%2fevil, \/\/evil and https://trusted.lab@evil bypass validation, yielding a 302 to an attacker host with the server-side fetch logged.

name: Server-side Document Rendering Injection
weakness: The PDF/document renderer loads user-controlled HTML with web security disabled and file access allowed, so injected JS reads file:///etc/passwd, performs SSRF to the internal-only service and executes inside the rendering context.

name: Regular Expression Denial of Service
weakness: Username validation uses the catastrophically-backtracking regex ^(a+)+$ with no input length or time limit; a short input returns in milliseconds while a crafted ~28-char input takes seconds (superlinear).

name: Weak Transport Layer Security
surface: TLS handshake sweep on :8743 + GET https://127.0.0.1:8743/
weakness: Server negotiates deprecated TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1 and weak CBC-SHA1 / static-RSA (no PFS) cipher suites at SECLEVEL=0, presents an expired self-signed hostname-mismatched RSA-1024/SHA1 certificate, and sends no HSTS.

name: Padding Oracle
weakness: AES-CBC with fixed key/IV returns distinguishable errors (500 'Padding error' vs 400 'Invalid data'), enabling a full byte-by-byte padding-oracle decryption of the vault token.

name: Sensitive Information Sent via Unencrypted Channels
surface: POST http://127.0.0.1:8700/login, GET /api/account (Basic auth), TCP :8723, https://127.0.0.1:8743/
weakness: Credentials, Basic-auth headers and API tokens cross plain HTTP/TCP; a TLS page submits its login form to an HTTP endpoint (mixed content) and session cookies lack the Secure flag.

name: Weak Cryptographic Primitives
weakness: Unsalted MD5 password hashes (reversible via precomputed lookup), AES-ECB revealing plaintext structure, static DES/RC4 keys decryptable to plaintext, and fixed-seed MT19937 reset tokens predictable via state clone.

name: Improper Error Handling
weakness: Failures leak SQL queries, schema, DB path and tracebacks and give enumerable distinct responses; conversely /api/transfer swallows all exceptions and returns 200 'success' while the operation actually failed.

name: Stack Traces
weakness: Unhandled exceptions in two stacks return full tracebacks with source paths, line numbers and framework internals; Werkzeug's interactive debugger (PIN-protected console) is exposed and Express runs in development mode.

name: Business Logic Data Validation
weakness: Quantity is never validated server-side: negative quantities produce a negative order total that is 'paid' as store credit, and a quantity of 1e9 is accepted against 10 units of stock.

name: Ability to Forge Requests
weakness: Checkout trusts client-supplied unit_price, shipping and grand total from hidden form fields, so a 500.00 item is purchased end-to-end for 0.01.

name: Integrity Checks
weakness: The order 'integrity' HMAC uses a hardcoded key leaked in client JS and is computed over the order id only, so a paid order's line items and total can be rewritten with a valid signature.

name: Process Timing
weakness: Single-use coupon redemption is check-then-act with no row lock: two genuinely parallel requests both redeem ONCE50 (uses=2, max_uses=1). The flash-sale window is evaluated against a client-supplied purchase_time, so an expired sale price is still accepted.

name: Number of Times a Function Can Be Used Limits
weakness: The 'one per customer' WELCOME5 promo is enforced with a session flag, not per account: the same account redeems it again from a fresh session/cookie jar.

name: Circumvention of Work Flows
weakness: Order confirmation never checks payment state, and fulfilment ships unpaid orders (and even order ids that do not exist), so mandatory workflow steps can be skipped or reordered.

name: Defenses Against Application Misuse
weakness: Gift-card redemption has no rate limiting, lockout or anomaly detection: a bounded 300-request sweep of the GC-XXXX space finds GC-1234 and credits the attacker's balance.

name: Upload of Unexpected File Types
weakness: Upload validation is a client-side accept attribute plus a lowercase .exe/.sh blacklist; a PHP payload named probe.php.jpg with Content-Type image/jpeg is stored and EXECUTED by the media host (AddHandler), and .html is served as text/html.

name: Upload of Malicious Files
weakness: The bulk-import pipeline joins raw zip entry names onto the target dir (zip-slip): a ../../pwned.php entry escapes the import directory into the web root and executes. A script-bearing SVG is accepted and served inline as image/svg+xml.

name: Payment Functionality
weakness: The payment intent amount is client-overridable (a 500.00 order is settled with a 0.01 intent), the 'succeeded' callback is unauthenticated and never reconciled (even for a nonexistent intent), and a negative refund extracts credit.

name: Denial of Inventory
weakness: Cart-add reserves stock with expires_at=NULL and no per-user cap; the expiry sweep never releases anything. An attacker holds all 3 units of the Limited Sneaker without paying and a legitimate buyer's checkout is rejected with 409.

name: DOM-Based Cross Site Scripting / Self DOM Based Cross Site Scripting
weakness: location.hash flows into innerHTML and location.search into document.write; a signature-preview field renders victim-typed HTML locally (Self-DOM-XSS, sub-doc 01.1). A nonce-based CSP variant blocks the self-XSS payload while the default page has no CSP.

name: JavaScript Execution
surface: GET /js-exec?expr=&cb=, new Function / setTimeout(string) buttons, GET /api/jsonp?callback=
weakness: eval(), new Function() and setTimeout(string) execute user input; the JSONP callback name is unsanitised so a callback of 'window.__jsonp_xss=1;//' runs arbitrary JS in the victim origin.

name: HTML Injection
weakness: User markup is reflected unencoded under a script-src 'none' CSP: injected scripts are blocked but spoofed content, forms and iframes render, and an injected credential form submits to the attacker origin.

name: Client-side URL Redirect
weakness: location.href is assigned the raw 'next' parameter with no allowlist and no scheme validation; navigation to the attacker origin and javascript: URLs are accepted by the sink.

name: CSS Injection
weakness: User-controlled CSS is injected into a <style> block on a page holding a secret token; attribute selectors plus url() callbacks exfiltrate the token's characters to the in-range attacker listener.

name: Client-side Resource Manipulation
weakness: The page loads a <script> (and iframe) whose src is taken straight from the URL, so attacker-controlled JS executes in the victim origin and reads its cookies.

name: Cross Origin Resource Sharing
weakness: Origin reflection with credentials, an unanchored prefix regex (http://127.0.0.1:8901 passes), an unanchored subdomain regex (trusted.lab.test.evil.com passes), Origin: null allowed with credentials, and ACAO:* on an unauthenticated PII endpoint. The attacker origin reads the victim's authenticated data in a real browser.

name: Clickjacking
weakness: The state-changing transfer form sends no X-Frame-Options and no frame-ancestors; the attacker origin frames it under a decoy button and a click on the decoy fires the authenticated transfer.

name: WebSockets
surface: WS /ws opened from the attacker origin
weakness: The WebSocket handshake performs no Origin check and authenticates by cookie only (SameSite=None), so a cross-origin page opens an authenticated socket (CSWSH) and performs a transfer; message content is acted on and echoed without sanitisation.

name: Web Messaging
surface: GET /messages framed by the attacker origin, postMessage both directions
weakness: The message receiver never validates event.origin and replies with targetOrigin '*': a cross-origin frame reads the victim's profile/CSRF token and triggers an authenticated email change.

name: Browser Storage
surface: GET /storage?note=, localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB, storage events across tabs
weakness: Session token, PII and card data are parked in localStorage, sessionStorage and IndexedDB; the page's DOM-XSS sink lets injected script read and exfiltrate them, and a storage-event handler propagates secrets to every other tab.

name: Cross Site Script Inclusion
surface: GET /api/private.js, /api/jsonp?callback=, /api/orders included via <script src> from the attacker origin
weakness: Authenticated sensitive data is served as includable JavaScript (a global variable and a JSONP callback), so a cross-origin <script> inclusion reads it without CORS. A top-level-array endpoint for the historical Array-constructor hijack is also provided (modern browsers use the intrinsic Array, so that variant no longer fires - documented in README).

name: Reverse Tabnabbing
weakness: Links open with an explicit rel=opener (and window.open without noopener) and no COOP header; the opened attacker page navigates window.opener.location to a phishing page on the attacker origin.

name: Client-side Template Injection
weakness: User input is reflected raw into an AngularJS 1.8.2 template (expression sandbox removed in 1.8); {{constructor.constructor('...')()}} executes arbitrary JS in the victim origin.

name: DOM Clobbering
weakness: The page reads window.config.href to choose a script src; an injected <a id=config href=attacker> clobbers the undefined global via named DOM access and loads attacker JS in the victim origin.

name: Cross-Site Leaks
surface: GET /dashboard framed cross-origin (window.length), GET /api/search?q= via <script> load/error events
weakness: Two real cross-site oracles: the dashboard's iframe count reveals authentication state through cross-origin window.length, and 200-vs-404 on a private-note search lets an attacker page recover secret digits via script load/error events.

name: Client-side Path Traversal
weakness: The client-side viewer concatenates user input into fetch('/api/files/'+doc); ../ segments are normalised by the browser into /api/admin/users, reaching an unintended endpoint that returns every user's PII.

name: Service Workers
weakness: An unauthenticated 'custom script' endpoint stores arbitrary same-origin JS served with Service-Worker-Allowed: /, and the page registers the URL-chosen script as a service worker with root scope; the worker intercepts and rewrites /api/data responses.

name: DNS Rebinding
surface: DNS rebind.lab.test (TTL 0) via :8953, Chromium through the :8908 rebinding proxy, http://rebind.lab.test:8902/
weakness: The authoritative lab DNS flips rebind.lab.test between the attacker container IP and the internal victim container IP with TTL 0; the internal service accepts any Host without auth. A real Chromium page loaded from the attacker phase reads the internal secret same-origin after the flip (resolution delegated to the in-range proxy).

name: API Reconnaissance
weakness: OpenAPI spec, a leftover Werkzeug route dump, an api-catalog metafile, JS comments and GraphQL introspection together enumerate far more endpoints than the UI uses, including an unauthenticated deprecated legacy endpoint and an undocumented v2 that still work.

name: API Broken Object Level Authorization
surface: GET+PUT /v1/orders/{id}, POST /v1/orders/update (id in body), GET /api/users/{id}/documents, GET+PUT /api/documents/{uuid}
weakness: No ownership checks: user A reads and modifies user B's order via the path id and via an order_id supplied in the JSON body; document UUIDs leaked by the listing endpoint grant read/write access to another user's documents.

name: Excessive Data Exposure
weakness: Responses return full model objects (password hashes, API tokens, SSNs, internal notes, other users' PII); app.js filters to username+email purely client-side. The undocumented v2 serializer embeds the complete owner record.

name: API Broken Function Level Authorization
weakness: The admin guard matches a path prefix plus write methods instead of the caller's role: GET /api/admin/users passes for any user, DELETE order has no role check, and role management outside /api/admin/ lets a normal user promote themselves to admin.

name: Inbound Webhooks
weakness: Receiver computes but ignores the provider HMAC, has no event_id/timestamp dedup (replays credit again), trusts the claimed account_id and amount, and fetches an attacker-supplied callback_url server-side, exposing an internal-only metadata service (SSRF).

name: gRPC
weakness: Server reflection enumerates services/methods and returns the .proto; the channel is plaintext with no auth; regular RPCs require an x-api-token but AdminDumpUsers/AdminSetStock enforce nothing, so anyone dumps password hashes and writes stock.

name: GraphQL
surface: POST /graphql (introspection, deep nesting, aliased login batch, updateOrderStatus, setUserRole)
weakness: Introspection on, no depth/complexity/alias limits, nested owner fields expose other users' hashes and tokens, aliased login mutations bypass the REST brute-force lockout, and mutations skip object-level and function-level authorization.

name: WebAssembly Reconnaissance
weakness: Two real clang-built modules (one disguised as .bin, lazy-loaded) retain the name section, DWARF debug info and a producers section identifying the toolchain; exports leak internal function names; data segments embed a live API key, an internal metadata URL and a build flag; the original C source is served alongside.
